title: Using Electron Energy-Gain Spectroscopy to Understand the Thermal Excitation of Plasmons in Complex Lithographically-Patterned Nanostructures
content: Next-generation monochromated and aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscope (MAC-STEM) has generated considerable interest in the field of nanoplasmonics, both in the visible [1] and the infrared [2]. Access to the IR enables measurement of phonon dispersions and vibrational spectra [3], but also gives access to thermal energy that influences properties in this regime. Large amounts of thermal energy are lost as low-grade heat that current technology fails to recover. We leveraged our previous experience imaging plasmons in the infrared to conduct in-situ heating of nanorods and observed a significant excitation of plasmons via electron energy gain spectroscopy (EEGS) [4]. In this manner, thermal energy can be extracted from a substrate and concentrated into an LSPR for subsequent use.
